newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 18.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Friday's Daily Variety:
* Former CBS Broadcast president Howard Stringer was officially named president of the newly configured Sony Corp of America, the U.S. unit of Sony Corp.

* Privately held movie distributor October Films agreed in principle to be acquired by Universal Studios, pending due diligence, sources said. No price was disclosed but insiders say it is under the firm's estimated value of $40 million.

* Executives at major U.S. theater chains said they had been warned unofficially by Viacom Paramount Pictures that James Cameron's high-budget "Titanic" would most likely not be released before July 18.
* With news that Tim Burton has signed on to develop "X -- The Man With X-Ray Eyes" as a project he would direct for DreamWorks and Orion Pictures, there now are three projects based on that premise.

* British Sky Broadcasting is rumored to be planning a new division, BSkyB Films, to invest in film production and possibly even build a studio in Britain. BSkyB would not confirm the plans, but the satellite broadcaster is said to be in internal discussions with 20th Century Fox over how to proceed. News Corp owns 40 percent of BSkyB.
* The unlikely partnership between General Electric NBC and Fox in the $40 million magazine strip "Access Hollywood" is starting to show signs of strain.
